question: TWO treatments, one panel. (a) Does a TYPED-EVENT table -- one-hot type x direction, counts over 1/5/21 sessions, magnitude, confidence and recency -- beat shuffled events, TF-IDF and no text? (b) Does the SCALAR construction the published event-return literature actually supports -- a single signed `direction x confidence` score, magnitude and the trailing counts, with the 43-way type identity DELIBERATELY absent -- beat the same controls and its own capacity-matched shuffle? Both under LightGBM and a StockMixer-class head, on purged walk-forward splits.

design.unit: (symbol, entry_date) cell -- one label per session, not one per headline
design.target: x_oc_h5 (SPY-excess cumulative return from the open of the first session after publication to the close of session +4)

feature_family.EVENT: typed_event_onehot_x_direction + magnitude + confidence + counts_1_5_21 + recency(+censored) + pit_price
feature_family.SCALAR: sc_dirconf (mean direction x confidence on the cell's own session) + sc_mag + counts over 1/5/21 sessions + pit_price. NO one-hot type column of any kind.

design.why_the_scalar_arm_exists: research_notes/2026-09-13/research_event_returns_last_read.md: E1's null conflated two hypotheses -- 'typed events do not work here' (what it tested, at h=5 with a 43-way one-hot block) and 'a scalar sentiment score at the literature's own horizon does not work here either' (never tested, because this file's HORIZONS excluded 1 and no arm dropped the one-hots). Both are now run on the same 26,003 typed rows at $0 marginal spend.

arms.EVENT: typed-event one-hot block + the three PIT price columns
arms.SCALAR: the five scalar columns + the three PIT price columns
arms.TFIDF: TF-IDF(1-2gram) -> 384-d SVD of the same text, fit on TRAIN rows only, per fold
arms.SHUFFLE: the EVENT block globally permuted across cells; price held fixed
arms.SCALAR_SHUFFLE: the SCALAR block under the SAME permutation -- the capacity-matched control for SCALAR, because a shuffled block with hundreds of noise columns overfits more and is a WEAKER opponent than five
arms.NOTEXT: log10 PIT 21-session median dollar volume, mom_21, mom_5

design.overlap_caveat: each date label spans 5 sessions and consecutive dates overlap; see `horizon_caveats` in the grade block.
design.splits: expanding walk-forward by month, 5-session embargo, first test month is month 7
design.book: decile long-short, EW, gross exposure 1.0, 3,000,000 PIT dollar-volume floor, charged on REALISED turnover sum|dw| x 25.0 bps
design.gbm_is_a_control: Lane M item M5 / Gu-Kelly-Xiu 2020. LightGBM is the bar the architecture must clear, not a competitor it may lose to quietly
design.typing: L2's typed rows (LLM extraction, frozen 40-id vocabulary). A verdict here is a verdict about typed events.
design.pit_rule_is_shared_by_both_arms: `build_scalar_features` uses the SAME searchsorted arithmetic as `build_features`: every window closes at the cell's own session, so no window can reach past it by construction rather than by a filter applied afterwards. The two arms differ in what they READ from the same rows.

panel.label: x_oc_h5
panel.label_definition: SPY-excess cumulative return, entry-session OPEN to the CLOSE of session +4 (5 sessions held)

bars_vintage.note: SPY open-to-close the panel subtracted vs SPY open-to-close in the local bars. False means the bars were re-pulled after the panel was built, so the label reconstruction gap below is a vintage gap, not a definition gap.

label_reconstruction_check.note: the panel's x_oc vs the same quantity rebuilt from the CURRENT bars. The SPY leg reconciles exactly; the difference is a bar-vintage revision on a handful of names, not a second label definition.

panel.dollar_vol_column_of_panel: IGNORED -- it is the entry session's own close x volume (not PIT)

features.proxy: typed by entity_tags where present and otherwise by a KEYWORD proxy over the 39-id vocabulary's own definitions and example headlines -- NOT by L2, which is not built

scalar_arm.no_one_hot: the 43-way type block is DELIBERATELY absent: this arm tests whether a signed scalar score carries the signal, which is the construction the published event-return literature supports and the one E1 had never run
scalar_arm.nan_policy: sc_dirconf and sc_mag are NaN when the cell has no same-session event -- LightGBM is NaN-native and a zero in a signed column would read as 'confidently neutral' rather than 'nothing happened'

shuffle_control.kind: global permutation of the treatment block across (symbol, entry_date); the SAME permutation is used for the EVENT block and for the SCALAR block
shuffle_control.note: labels, dates, universe, construction and the PIT price columns are identical; only the event-to-cell link is cut
shuffle_control.why_two_shuffles: SHUFFLE carries 300 shuffled columns and SCALAR_SHUFFLE carries 5. A bigger block of pure noise overfits more and is a WEAKER opponent, so grading SCALAR against SHUFFLE alone would flatter it. Each treatment is read against its own capacity-matched shuffle as well as the three shared controls.

source_meta.entry_date_rule: a PANEL row uses the panel's OWN entry_date for every cell carrying its text; a CORPUS row uses the first panel session STRICTLY AFTER the document's own date, conservative by one for a pre-open headline
source_meta.dedupe_key: (symbol, entry_date, text_sha256); panel files read first

typing_coverage.note: entity_tags contribute 0 on the 2025-26 panel: the tagged corpus starts 2026-09-11 and this panel predates it. The path is live and will show a number the day the corpus reaches back.

results.holm_family_note: declared at 14 before the read (two treatments x 2 model(s) x the three shared controls plus each treatment's own matched shuffle); 14 leg(s) produced a p-value. SCALAR_minus_EVENT and the architecture comparison are head-to-heads and are reported OUTSIDE the family.

horizon_caveats.overlap_note: each date label spans 5 sessions, so consecutive dates share 4 of them. The reported n of 280 is NOT 280 independent observations: it is about 56. Divide every t in this receipt by roughly sqrt(5) = 2.24 before reading it as significance, and treat a per-era cell with fewer than 5 dates as CANNOT DETERMINE.
horizon_caveats.annualisation_note: ann_pct in every cell is mean x 252 x 100 of that daily series. At horizon 5 it counts the same capital about 5 times over; divide by 5 for a first-order comparable figure. IC is horizon-agnostic and is the number to use for any cross-horizon comparison.

verdict: FAILED_VARIANT: NEITHER treatment -- the 43-way one-hot type block NOR the scalar direction x confidence score the published literature uses -- beats its own capacity-matched shuffled control under any model, so what either earns is the panel's calendar and universe, not the events. This closes THIS READ of the LLM-typed rows at 32,384 of 130,719 cells (24.8% coverage); below ~5% coverage the shuffled control has little power, and the next test is typing the panel's own headlines, not another head.
next_test: L2's LLM extraction over the same cells, graded through this identical table, splits, book and controls -- the ONLY difference being how the events were typed. That is what separates 'typed events do not work here' from 'a keyword proxy does not work here'.
